tldr: New sparse-cache drafting, AMD inference benchmarking and document parsing tools offer practical routes to evaluate inference efficiency, while small-model team training and reasoning-trace mining explore better use of limited compute.

Research on visual helper images and speech fillers highlights the need for targeted evaluation; Swiss authorities confirm attacker-directed agent-assisted incidents, reinforcing conventional defensive controls.

news.title: Tencent extends DFly2 drafting to three sparse-attention model families
news.summary: AngelSpec's November 26 entry announces training code, draft checkpoints and a report for DFly2, including new drafts for Hy4 flash, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash and GLM-5.3-Flash. Draft layers reuse target attention cache and selected token indices.
news.why_it_matters: Could reduce redundant computation for long-context speculative generation when the target and serving engine support sharing.
news.caveat: Checkpoint page inaccessible during this review; actual downloads, license terms and serving compatibility not verified. Acceptance length and decoding speed do not establish end-to-end latency.

news.title: Public llama.cpp benchmark dashboard tracks AMD local inference
news.summary: The ggml team introduced a dashboard comparing prompt processing and generation across AMD hardware, model formats and llama.cpp builds. The announcement describes weekly workflows, ten repetitions per configuration and public raw results.
news.why_it_matters: Makes regression diagnosis and hardware/model tradeoffs easier to inspect instead of relying on a single tokens-per-second number.
news.caveat: Results cover tested hardware and builds; not a general AMD-versus-NVIDIA ranking. Dashboard execution not independently tested.

news.title: NVIDIA shares document parsing training recipe and DFlash2 draft
news.summary: NVIDIA describes synthetic training data, supervised tuning and verifiable-reward RL for Nemotron 3.5 Parse, plus a DFlash2 draft. On one H200 in BF16, reported throughput gains over the non-speculative 3.5 configuration are 7.62x at concurrency 1 and 1.52x at 512.
news.why_it_matters: A documented route to adapt structured document extraction and assess whether speculation improves serving cost.
news.caveat: Vendor benchmarks on selected pages and accelerator; extraction errors remain possible. Artifact terms and deployment not independently tested.

news.title: Hugging Face demonstrates reinforcement learning for four 0.6B agents
news.summary: A shared Qwen3-0.6B policy was trained for a cooperative number-ordering task with four logical agents. The authors report 26 of 32 held-out tasks solved at update 75 and a 37.4% decline in generated tokens per team between early and late training windows.
news.why_it_matters: Provides a small-model team-training example with explicit communication and compute accounting.
news.caveat: Toy task, small holdout, and token savings measured during training rather than held-out inference. Original run used eight GPUs; cannot infer general software-engineering superiority.

news.title: Generated helper images often hurt visual reasoning in tested systems
news.summary: Across 13 model-generator pairings, adding generated visual aids reduced mean answer accuracy by 3.7 percentage points; nine of ten tasks declined.
news.why_it_matters: Suggests testing intermediate visual artifacts against text-only planning and no-generation baselines.
news.caveat: Selected models and tasks; not evidence that all visual reasoning or image generation is harmful.
news.publication_date_basis: v1 submitted November 25; listed November 26; exact public posting time unverified

news.title: Theoretical work establishes limits on optimal tokenizer approximation
news.summary: The authors prove conditional hardness results for direct and bottom-up tokenizer optimization under compression and unigram-likelihood objectives, ruling out constant-factor polynomial approximation for the specified formulations unless P equals NP.
news.why_it_matters: Explains why practical tokenizer construction may require heuristics rather than efficient universally optimal algorithms.
news.caveat: Theoretical objectives and worst-case complexity, not a claim that existing tokenizers are ineffective or all practical corpora are hard.
news.publication_date_basis: v1 submitted November 25; listed November 26; exact public posting time unverified

news.title: DART mines useful alternatives from rejected reasoning traces
news.summary: DART selects uncertain steps of failed mathematical reasoning and branches into alternative completions with answer guidance. Authors report recovering 37% more previously unsolved problems than independent sampling at equal trace counts.
news.why_it_matters: Potentially expands post-training coverage of difficult examples rather than discarding failed traces.
news.caveat: Reference-answer guidance and verifier quality matter; comparable trace count does not establish equal token cost or broad generalization.
news.publication_date_basis: v1 submitted November 25; listed November 26; exact public posting time unverified

news.title: DexLink builds dexterous robot policies from reusable pose templates
news.summary: The framework retargets reusable hand-object interaction poses, links them into reference trajectories and refines behavior using residual RL in simulation.
news.why_it_matters: Could reduce the need for object-specific demonstrations in manipulation research.
news.caveat: Author experiments and preliminary transfer results; no broad real-world reliability or safety certification.
news.publication_date_basis: v1 submitted November 25; listed November 26; exact public posting time unverified

news.title: Frozen speech recognizer recovers omitted verbal fillers
news.summary: UMAI combines frame-level outputs and decoder states from Qwen3-ASR-1.7B to insert hesitation tags without changing recognized words. On held-out AMI, reported filler F1 improves from 12.2 to 82.6, with 14% extra processing time.
news.why_it_matters: Useful for verbatim dialogue datasets and conversational timing analysis without modifying the base recognizer.
news.caveat: Threshold selected on a separate benchmark; F1 measures filler detection, not overall transcription quality or universal speaker performance.
news.publication_date_basis: v1 submitted November 25; listed November 26; exact public posting time unverified

news.title: Providing relevant mathematical theory improves constrained LLM problem solving
news.summary: In a length-matched experiment on pattern waiting-time problems, Qwen3-14B pass@1 rose from 0.37 to 0.83 with a relevant theory in context; the reported median correct-solution length also fell.
news.why_it_matters: Motivates testing compact reusable domain knowledge rather than merely extending prompts with examples.
news.caveat: Narrow problem family and oracle theory condition; results shrink with solver size and token budget.
news.publication_date_basis: v1 submitted November 25; listed November 26; exact public posting time unverified

news.title: Swiss cyber authority confirms agent-assisted intrusions
news.summary: Swiss NCSC confirmed compromises involving attacker-directed AI assistance against organizations including critical infrastructure. Reuters subsequently reported an updated case count attributed to the federal authority.
news.why_it_matters: Supports prioritizing patching, access controls, MFA and incident detection in exposed systems.
news.caveat: November 24 government notice and November 26 Reuters update differ in case scope; exact incident dates and attribution are not established here. Not evidence of independent AI intent.

news.title: ClickHouse announces expanded five-year AWS data-stack agreement
news.summary: ClickHouse announced a framework for more than $1.5 billion in potential investment over five years, including planned integration with AWS agent services and real-time enterprise data.
news.why_it_matters: Highlights growing demand for data access, tracing and evaluation infrastructure around production agents.
news.caveat: Agreement framework is not realized expenditure; planned integrations and preview features are not general availability.

terms.name: Filled pause
terms.definition: A voiced hesitation, such as um or uh, that occupies a pause in speech without adding ordinary propositional content.
terms.mechanism: A speaker vocalizes during planning or hesitation; ASR can detect these events separately from lexical words using acoustic and contextual features.
terms.example: A verbatim recognizer preserves the hesitation in 'I, um, agree' rather than outputting only 'I agree'.
terms.caveat: Not newly coined; some transcription conventions intentionally remove fillers, and detection is not a direct measurement of emotion or intent.
